quick: Progestin-only pill: 4 mg orally once daily for 24 days then 4 days inactive tablets (28-day cycle); combined products contain 3 mg with ethinyl estradiol
Take with food if nausea occurs; take at the same time each day
Contraindicated - not for use in pregnancy
Small amounts pass into milk; may slightly reduce milk volume; generally considered compatible with established breastfeeding
Contraindicated in renal impairment due to hyperkalemia risk
Contraindicated in hepatic impairment / active liver disease or tumor
Serum potassium in at-risk patients during first cycle; blood pressure; bleeding pattern; thrombosis signs
summary: Drospirenone is a unique progestin structurally derived from spironolactone, with antimineralocorticoid and antiandrogenic activity. It is used alone as a progestin-only oral contraceptive (4 mg daily) and combined with an estrogen (3 mg) for combined hormonal contraception and other indications. Its antimineralocorticoid effect counteracts estrogen-related fluid retention but creates a risk of hyperkalemia, so it is contraindicated in renal/hepatic/adrenal insufficiency and used cautiously with other potassium-raising drugs. Like other hormonal contraceptives, it carries thromboembolic risk.
indications: Prevention of pregnancy in combination with an estrogen (combined oral contraceptive, 3 mg drospirenone)
As part of combined products, treatment of moderate acne and premenstrual dysphoric disorder (product/region specific)

dosage.r: Adult / post-menarche female of reproductive potential
dosage.t: One active tablet daily for 24 days, then one inactive tablet daily for 4 days (28-day pack)
dosage.n: Take at the same time each day; missed-pill rules apply

dosage.d: 3 mg drospirenone + ethinyl estradiol once daily
dosage.t: Daily per pack regimen (e.g., 21 active + 7 inactive, or 24/4)

admin: Take one tablet by mouth at the same time every day
Follow the pack order; do not skip the inactive (placebo) days
If a dose is delayed or missed, follow the missed-pill instructions in the product leaflet
If vomiting or severe diarrhea occurs within a few hours of a dose, treat as a missed pill
moa: Drospirenone is a synthetic progestogen that suppresses ovulation, thickens cervical mucus, and alters the endometrium to prevent pregnancy. Unlike most progestins it is an analogue of spironolactone with antimineralocorticoid activity (antagonizing aldosterone, promoting sodium/water excretion and potassium retention) and antiandrogenic activity (it does not have estrogenic, glucocorticoid, or antiglucocorticoid activity).

absolute: Current or history of venous or arterial thromboembolic disease (for combined estrogen-containing products)
Hepatic impairment, active liver disease, or liver tumor (benign or malignant)
Known or suspected hormone-sensitive (e.g., breast) malignancy
relative: Concomitant use of potassium-sparing diuretics, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, aldosterone antagonists, NSAIDs, or potassium supplements (hyperkalemia)
Risk factors for venous/arterial thrombosis (especially combined products)
Migraine, hypertension, smoking over age 35 (combined products)
monitor: Serum potassium in patients at risk during the first treatment cycle

preg: Drospirenone is contraindicated in pregnancy; it is a contraceptive and should be stopped if pregnancy occurs. Epidemiologic studies have not shown an increased risk of birth defects when hormonal contraceptives are taken inadvertently during early pregnancy.
lact: Small amounts of drospirenone are excreted in human milk. Hormonal contraception may decrease milk production, particularly when breastfeeding is not well established; the progestin-only pill is generally preferred over combined products during lactation.
renal: Drospirenone is contraindicated in patients with renal impairment because reduced renal potassium excretion increases the risk of hyperkalemia from its antimineralocorticoid activity.
hepatic: Drospirenone is contraindicated in patients with hepatic impairment or active liver disease, as hepatic metabolism may be impaired and liver function can be affected by hormonal contraceptives.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St. John's wort) reduce contraceptive efficacy
Combination of drugs raising serum potassium (ACE inhibitors, ARBs, aldosterone antagonists, potassium-sparing diuretics, chronic NSAIDs, potassium supplements, heparin)
moderate: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin) may increase drospirenone exposure
Some antiretrovirals and HCV protease inhibitors may alter hormone levels
Lamotrigine (combined products may lower lamotrigine levels)
minor: Possible modest increase in exposure of other CYP-metabolized hormones
interactions.food: May be taken with food to reduce nausea; no major food interaction
interactions.diagnostics: May affect levels of some binding proteins and clotting/thyroid/liver test values; inform laboratory

serious: Hyperkalemia (especially with renal impairment or potassium-raising drugs)
emergency: Signs of pulmonary embolism (sudden breathlessness, chest pain)
Signs of stroke or heart attack

monitoring: Serum potassium during the first cycle in patients on potassium-raising drugs or with mild renal impairment
Bleeding pattern and pregnancy status if missed doses
counsel: Take one tablet at the same time each day in the pack order
Use back-up contraception when you miss pills or have vomiting/diarrhea, per the leaflet
Tell your doctor about kidney problems and any medicines that raise potassium
Seek urgent care for chest pain, shortness of breath, severe leg pain/swelling, or stroke symptoms
Hormonal contraceptives do not protect against sexually transmitted infections
Irregular bleeding is common in the first months and usually settles
pk: Contraceptive effect established within the first cycle when started as directed
Peak plasma concentration about 1-2 hours after an oral dose
Store at room temperature; protect from moisture
pearls: Only progestin with antimineralocorticoid activity - 4 mg approximates the potassium effect of 25 mg spironolactone
Antiandrogenic activity makes drospirenone-containing combined pills useful for acne and hirsutism
Hyperkalemia risk drives the contraindication in renal/hepatic/adrenal insufficiency - check potassium in at-risk users
Progestin-only 4 mg formulation has a 24/4 regimen and a more forgiving missed-pill window than older progestin-only pills
Counteracts estrogen-related fluid retention, which may reduce bloating compared with other combined pills
missed: If a tablet is taken more than 24 hours late or missed, take it as soon as remembered and take the next at the usual time (even two on one day); follow the product-specific missed-pill rules and use back-up contraception for 7 days if active tablets were missed. Missing tablets during the active phase increases the chance of pregnancy.
overdose: No serious harmful effects have been reported from overdose. Symptoms may include nausea, vomiting, and in females vaginal bleeding. There is no specific antidote; treatment is supportive. Monitor serum potassium if large amounts were ingested, particularly in patients with renal impairment.
